inputs.modified_text:
Folks, once again we see the fundamental breakdown of law and order when soft-headed judicial logic ties the hands of justice. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has laid down a ruling—courtesy of Justice Sumeet Goel—declaring that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Instead, they demand "clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances." 

Think about what this means for the basic security of our homes and neighborhoods. When a court dismisses a plea seeking the cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...] trespass or theft-related matter just because the stolen goods haven't been recovered, it sends all the wrong signals to criminals. It undermines the authority of the law and abandons the victims of crime in favor of procedural loopholes. We need an unwavering commitment to public safety, traditional family security, and strict accountability—not judges making it easier for suspects to stay out of custody while property remains unrecovered and victims wait for justice.
